text: you should just set them so that they have a random goal oriented behavior. use every intersection as a point. set a point for them to travel to that is not the immediate next one, set them with distance so that the car behavior doesnt feel fixed
resolution: Replaced the closed-loop tracer (which found the SMALLEST cycle, so every car circled the nearest intersection) with goal-oriented routing per the user's direction: junctions are the nodes, each car drives a TOUR of several random DISTANT intersections (>=minGoalMeters away, varied leg count) then home, so it loops without teleporting and feels un-fixed. Each leg is a real shortest legal path via directed BFS (on-road, never against lane flow). Load-bearing fix: the routing passability mask now means DRIVABLE (traversable + finite vehicleCost) not PREFERRED — crosswalk tiles at every intersection are not 'preferred', so the old mask sealed lanes off from junctions (0 routable tours); including them connects the network and all 14 cars route across the whole city. 9/9 traffic tests; re-baked + self-shot — 14 cars spread across the map on varied routes, no clustering. SHA 63902d3f8.
